newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Aug tax receipts fall but cash up - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia Aug tax receipts fall but cash up - minister.

text.p: Russian federal government tax recepits fell in August in rouble terms from July levels, but the government received more actual cash, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Tuesday.
Tax receipts were 15.10 trillion roubles in August, down from 18.70 trillion roubles in July, he told a news conference.
But the volume of real money in August was 13.50 trillion roubles after 8.60 trillion roubles in July, with tax exemptions making up the difference.
The government issues tax exemptions to factories, which can use them to pay their taxes to the federal government, producing no real revenues.

"This important change took place because tax exemption issues were mostly exhausted in June and July," Yasin said, adding that in June and July more than 50 percent of all taxes were in the form of tax exemptions.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF)strongly objected to the tax exemption system. The IMF said the system had undermined fiscal policy and delayed the release of the July tranche of its $10 billion loan because it was worried about Russia's ability to meet revenue targets.
The IMF released the July tranche last month.
Yasin also said 40 percent of all income in Russia was hidden from taxation.
